[page[title]]

Expression-bodied method implementations must start on the line after the => token.

What The Standard says

“Readability” — The Standard prioritizes readability. Placing a multiline expression body below the arrow gives the implementation a stable visual entry point. read it here.
“Abstraction” — The Standard's broker implementations repeatedly place multiline expression-bodied calls on the line after the arrow. The analyser codifies that canonical presentation. read it here.

Why it matters

Placing a multiline expression body below the arrow keeps the expression's structure visible and consistent with other wrapped constructs. The analyser turns the Standard's readability principle into one predictable layout for long implementations.

Bad code example

// Violates STXFORMAT002: Expression-bodied method implementations must start on the line after the => token.
ValueTask<Student> GetStudent() => service.GetStudent();

Good code example

// Follows STXFORMAT002
ValueTask<Student> GetStudent() =>
    service.GetStudent();
